outline: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Phyllodes tumors are biphasic fibroepithelial breast neoplasms in which the neoplastic stromal component grows around epithelial-lined spaces and forms characteristic leaf-like projections. Stromal cellularity, atypia, mitotic activity, overgrowth, and the tumor border are major histologic features used in grading.
vignette: A 47-year-old woman presents with a painless breast mass that has enlarged rapidly over several months. Examination shows a large, firm, mobile mass. Mammography demonstrates a round, lobulated, predominantly circumscribed lesion. Core biopsy shows a biphasic lesion containing benign ductal epithelium and a markedly cellular stromal component.
lead: Which additional microscopic finding would most strongly support the suspected diagnosis?
correct: Leaf-like stromal projections extending into elongated epithelial-lined clefts
distractors: Uniform relatively hypocellular stroma surrounding open glands in a pericanalicular pattern
Papillary fronds with fibrovascular cores covered by epithelial and myoepithelial cells
Atypical epithelial cells invading through the basement membrane into desmoplastic stroma
Necrotic adipocytes surrounded by foamy macrophages with later fibrosis or calcification
distractor_notes: A relatively uniform pericanalicular or intracanalicular stromal pattern without the characteristic leaf-like architecture is typical of fibroadenoma, the principal benign fibroepithelial differential diagnosis.
Fibrovascular cores lined by epithelial and myoepithelial cells characterize intraductal papilloma, which is an epithelial papillary lesion rather than a stromal fibroepithelial neoplasm.

Invasive ductal carcinoma is an epithelial malignancy defined by neoplastic epithelial cells breaching the basement membrane and infiltrating breast stroma; this does not match the biphasic benign-epithelium/cellular-stroma pattern in the vignette.

Breast fat necrosis shows injured/necrotic adipocytes with foamy histiocytes or macrophages and evolves toward fibrosis and sometimes calcification; it is an inflammatory reparative lesion rather than a leaf-forming fibroepithelial tumor.
key_expl: The rapidly enlarging breast mass and biphasic lesion with benign epithelium plus markedly cellular stroma suggest a phyllodes tumor. The defining architecture is an exaggerated intracanalicular pattern in which hypercellular stromal fronds project into elongated epithelial-lined spaces, producing a leaf-like appearance. Fibroadenoma is the closest differential but generally has more uniform, less cellular stroma and lacks the characteristic leaf-like stromal architecture.
objective: Differentiate phyllodes tumor from other breast lesions by recognizing its biphasic fibroepithelial composition and characteristic leaf-like projections formed by cellular stromal fronds.
clues: biphasic benign epithelium plus cellular stroma

sources.support: Phyllodes tumors are fibroepithelial neoplasms with stromal and epithelial components; microscopically they show enhanced intracanalicular growth with leaf-like stromal projections into epithelial-lined clefts. Stromal cellularity, atypia, mitotic activity, stromal overgrowth, and margins contribute to grading, and clinically these tumors commonly present as enlarging painless breast masses.
